clips.title: Zod Goes Where TypeScript Can't
clips.why: Theo explains the gap this lesson closes: TypeScript cannot see data that arrives while the program runs.
look: The limits of TypeScript: types are gone at run time.
Parsing with a zod schema, and getting the inferred type from it.
clips.after: Every model answer, request body and file the platform reads crosses that gap, so each one goes through a schema.

clips.title: Learn Zod In 30 Minutes
clips.why: The basic zod workflow, slowly and clearly: a schema, parse and safeParse, and z.infer.
look: The difference between parse, which throws, and safeParse, which returns success or the problems.
z.infer giving the TypeScript type from the schema.
clips.after: The broker uses safeParse on every scope it receives, and the readiness check uses parse on the model's answer.

clips.title: Zod 4 is out, and it is CRAZY
clips.why: Thirty-five seconds on the zod 4 feature the platform relies on to talk to models: JSON Schema straight from a zod schema.
look: z.toJSONSchema turning a schema into JSON Schema, with no extra library.
clips.after: The readiness check and the planner hand that JSON Schema to the model as outputFormat, then parse the answer with the same schema.

practice.q: Why did JSON.parse(text) as Readiness let "Ready" through?

options.text: Because as only tells the compiler what to assume; nothing checks the value at run time
options.why: Types disappear when the code runs. Only a schema that runs, such as Readiness.safeParse, looks at the real value.
JSON.parse keeps strings exactly as written. "Ready" stays "Ready".
The type is a union of string literals, and it is exact. It just does not exist when the code runs.

practice.q: Get the TypeScript type from the schema, so the two can never drift apart.
practice.hint: zod reads the schema and works out the type.
practice.why: z.infer turns the schema into the matching type. Change the schema and the type follows.

practice.q: POST /v1/comments receives a body that does not match the Comment schema. What should the route do?

options.text: Comment.parse and let the throw become a 500
options.why: A bad body is the caller's mistake, not a bug in the service. 500 would point people at the wrong place.

options.text: Comment.safeParse and answer 400 with z.prettifyError of the problems
options.why: safeParse never throws, and the readable problems tell the caller exactly which field to fix.

options.text: Store it anyway and clean it up later
options.why: Data that was never checked spreads through the system. The door is the cheapest place to stop it.

practice.q: Hand the same schema to the model as JSON Schema.
practice.hint: zod 4 can write JSON Schema for you.
practice.why: One schema gives the type, tells the model what to write, and checks the answer with Readiness.parse.

practice.q: Put the readiness check in order.
items: Describe the verdict once as a zod schema
Turn it into JSON Schema with z.toJSONSchema
Ask the model to answer in that shape
Parse the model's structured_output with the same schema
Branch on the checked verdict: ready, ask or hand_back
practice.why: The schema is both the request to the model and the check of its answer. Only checked data reaches the branch.
